content.text: No audit, inspection, or verification right binding the Client exists anywhere in the agreement. The only verification-type mechanic runs in our favour (§6 documentation on request; §3(e) usage statistics access to us).

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right against Mortgage Logic.com. Sections 5-6 (compensation), 7 (spamming), 8 (Client covenants), 10 (confidentiality) and 2-4 (license/services) were reviewed and contain no such right, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "examine", "verif", "monitor" and "premises" returned nothing. The only verification-style mechanics run in our favour: §6 entitles us to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them, and §3(e) gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. The nearest counterparty rights are §8(f) (TrueLink may implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming) and §9 (we provide access so TrueLink can make Y2K repairs at its own cost) — neither is an audit of our usage and both are narrow/self-funded by TrueLink. Silence is better than the preferred position (no frequency, notice, cost or system-access exposure), so no redline is warranted; we should not introduce an audit right against ourselves.
